items.good: The file opens with a comment telling what the workflow does (runs the tests on Linux and macOS on every push, on the oldest and the latest Python) and why it is there (so the pull request shows each behavior holds on both), before any of its body; YAML has no functions or tests of its own, so the module opening is the whole of the template that applies.

The workflow uses only what the development rules name: ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (architecture.md:129-130), pipx install ./organize-downloads and PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests in organize-downloads (architecture.md:131-132), on Python 3.10, the oldest pyproject.toml's requires-python names, and on the latest 3.x; the check step uses only grep, sed -E with POSIX classes, printf and bash's test, which both runners have. I ran the install and test steps on Linux, on Python 3.10.22 and 3.14.4 (pipx through uvx, its home in a mktemp folder): both installed the tool and ran 65 tests, OK. On GitHub, run 40408267138 of HEAD, with the same pinned SHAs and the same install and test steps, passed all four jobs, 65 tests each; the remade file, with its check step, is not pushed yet, so no GitHub run of it exists, and the check was run here on GNU tools only, not on macOS's.

Each stop of the check step names the condition and both values and gives an action that clears it. I ran lines 30-43 with ${{ matrix.python }} filled in, on a copy of pyproject.toml in a mktemp folder: as is with 3.10, exit 0; with the matrix at 3.10 and requires-python written as ">=3.9", ">=3.9,<4", '>=3.9', ">= 3.9", requires-python=">=3.9", "<4,>=3.9" and "!=3.9.1, >=3.9", each exit 1 saying Make the first python of this workflow's matrix "3.9", and each exit 0 once the matrix is 3.9; with "~=3.9", ">3.8" or no requires-python line, exit 1 saying to give it as ">=<version>", after which the first message leads on; with ">=3.9.2", it names "3.9.2" and passes once the matrix is that. The rest of the workflow's stops are cleared by what they say: a failing test shows its own message, such as test_stories' INSTALL_HINT, whose condition the install step meets, and the repository's refusal of unpinned actions (run 40407523124) is cleared by lines 18-22, both actions being pinned so.

parts.good: Each decision is told where it is made: lines 1-2 why there are two systems and two Pythons; lines 14-15 that the first Python is the one requires-python names and which step checks it; line 10 why fail-fast is false; lines 18-22 why each action is a full SHA, which the repository's policy demands (checked: run 40407523124 was refused for @v7), that the comment beside it names its release, and how to update both. I ran that `git ls-remote <url> refs/tags/<release>*` for v7.0.1 of actions/checkout and v7.1.0 of actions/setup-python: it printed 3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 and 6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0, the SHAs on lines 24 and 44, the newest tags of each; on git/git's annotated v2.40.0 it printed the tag and its ^{} line as the comment says. Lines 25-26 say why the check step is there; line 32 says what the sed expression on line 33 takes, which my runs above bore out; the step's name and its `if` tell what it checks and on which job. Line 47 says why pipx, line 52 why PYTHONPATH=src. No comment tells how the work went.

Every key serves the asked behavior (AC7: the tests on macOS and Linux on every push, on the oldest and latest Python): one trigger, one job, the matrix, the two pinned actions, the check that the matrix's oldest Python is the one pyproject.toml requires (its `if` needed, as 3.x names no version to compare; its two messages each the action for a different stop), one install step and one test step; no option or case for a future. Each comment gives a reason or a meaning the line under it does not show.

items.good: The oldest Python, written both in the matrix and in pyproject.toml's requires-python, can no longer be changed in one place and left old in the other: lines 14-15 name the other place, and the check step fails the 3.10 jobs where they differ, whatever form requires-python is written in (runs under B-2). The SHA and its release comment sit on one line and lines 18-22 say to change them together, and the ignore file keeps out __pycache__/, build/ and *.egg-info/, which the install and test steps make.

The test step runs every test module (unittest discover -s tests: test_cli, test_folder, test_organize, test_type_table, test_stories) on both systems and both Pythons, and the install step makes the stories run the command as pipx installs it, which test_stories' test_the_command_on_path_runs_the_code_under_test checks is the code in src. In run 40408267138 each job ran 65 tests; the one skipped on macOS is the Linux-only settings story, with the reason written beside it (test_stories.py:171-173), and the root-only skip in test_cli.py:213-215 says GitHub Actions does not run as root.

With fail-fast false each system and Python is its own job, named test (<os>, <python>), so a failure points to the one system and Python it came from and does not hide another; the version check is a step of its own, named for what it checks, so its failure is not read as a test's. The install and test steps already pass (run 40408267138: four jobs, success), and the check passes on the pyproject.toml as it is (run here: exit 0), so a failure after a change is that change's.

The test step ran 65 tests in 0.26-0.37 s on each job of run 40408267138, and in about 0.1 s here; the whole run took 45 s, the one setup beyond the tests being one pipx install per job, not per test, and the version check a grep and a sed.

Each job runs on its own fresh runner and writes only into its own checkout, its own pipx folders and the temporary folders the tests make; the check step writes nothing. So jobs of one push, or runs of two pushes at once, share no place they write.

chosen.chosen: Pinned actions/checkout to v7.0.1 (3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1) and actions/setup-python to v7.1.0 (6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0).
chosen.why: Each is the latest published release of its action, and the very commit the tag v7 that T3's workflow used names now, so the workflow runs what T3 meant, only pinned.

chosen.chosen: The version is written as a trailing comment of the form `# v7.0.1` on the same line as the SHA, with one comment above the steps saying why SHAs are used and to change both together.
chosen.why: The task asks for the version in a comment beside each SHA; one line per action keeps a hand update to one edit, and stating the rule once above the steps keeps it out of each line.

chosen.chosen: The comment above the steps gives `git ls-remote <action's repository URL> refs/tags/<release>*` as the way to find a release's commit SHA, taking the ^{} line where two are printed.
chosen.why: The user decided updates are made by hand; this command needs only git, which the README already asks for, and for an annotated tag the plain line is the tag object's SHA, not a commit's, which the repository's rule would stop.

chosen.chosen: The oldest Python is tied to requires-python by a step on every job but the latest-Python ones (`if: matrix.python != '3.x'`) that takes the version after ">=" from the requires-python line with grep and sed and fails where the matrix's first python differs, rather than by a first job that reads requires-python and hands the version to the matrix.
chosen.why: grep and sed need no other job, checkout or Python before the matrix (tomllib is missing on Python 3.10), and the step fails naming both values and the fix, while a job feeding the matrix would add a job to every push and, where it read nothing, hand setup-python an empty version; reading the ">=" bound in any quoting, spacing or beside other bounds lets every valid way of writing the same oldest version pass.
